s: Israel's descendants multiply in Egypt. A new Pharaoh enslaves them and orders their baby boys killed.
Moses is born, hidden in a basket on the Nile and raised by Pharaoh's daughter. He kills an Egyptian and flees to Midian.
God speaks to Moses from a burning bush, reveals his name, I AM WHO I AM, and sends him to free his people.
God gives Moses signs to perform and appoints Aaron to speak for him. Moses returns to Egypt.
Moses and Aaron ask Pharaoh to let the people go. Pharaoh refuses and makes their labour harsher.
God promises again to free Israel and take them as his people. The family line of Moses and Aaron is recorded.
Aaron's staff becomes a serpent before Pharaoh. The first plague turns the Nile to blood.
Plagues of frogs, gnats and flies strike Egypt, but Pharaoh's heart stays hard.
Plagues of disease on the livestock, boils and hail fall on Egypt.
Locusts and darkness cover Egypt. Pharaoh still refuses to let the people go.
God announces the last plague, the death of every firstborn in Egypt.
God institutes the Passover: a lamb without blemish is killed and its blood marks each door. At midnight the firstborn die, and Israel leaves Egypt.
The firstborn are set apart for God and the feast of Unleavened Bread is fixed. God leads the people by a pillar of cloud and fire.
Pharaoh pursues Israel. God parts the Red Sea for his people, and the waters return over the Egyptian army.
Moses and Miriam sing a song of victory. In the desert God makes bitter water sweet.
The people complain of hunger, and God sends quail and manna, bread from heaven, with a double portion before the sabbath.
God gives water from the rock. Israel defeats Amalek while Moses holds up his hands in prayer.
Moses' father-in-law Jethro visits and advises him to share the work of judging the people.
Israel camps at Mount Sinai. God offers a covenant to make them his own people, and comes down on the mountain in thunder and fire.
God gives the Ten Commandments. The people, afraid, ask Moses to speak to God for them.
Laws about servants, violence, injury and responsibility.
Laws about property, theft, and care for the stranger, the widow and the poor.
Laws about justice and honesty, the sabbath year, and the three yearly feasts. God promises to lead them into the land.
The covenant is sealed with the blood of sacrifice. Moses goes up the mountain for forty days.
God asks for offerings to build his sanctuary and gives the design of the ark of the covenant, the table and the lampstand.
Instructions for the tabernacle, its curtains, frames and veil.
Instructions for the altar of sacrifice and the courtyard around the tabernacle.
Instructions for the priestly garments of Aaron and his sons.
How the priests are to be consecrated, and the daily offering of two lambs.
The altar of incense, the census tax, the bronze basin, and the holy anointing oil and incense.
God fills Bezalel with skill to make everything for the tabernacle. The sabbath is a lasting sign of the covenant.
While Moses is on the mountain the people make a golden calf and worship it. Moses intercedes for them, and the guilty are punished.
God speaks with Moses face to face in the tent of meeting, and shows him his glory passing by.
God renews the covenant and Moses carves new tablets. His face shines after speaking with the Lord.
The people bring generous gifts for the tabernacle, more than enough.
The craftsmen make the tabernacle's curtains and frames.
Bezalel makes the ark, the table, the lampstand and the altar of incense.
The altar of sacrifice, the bronze basin and the courtyard are made, and the materials are counted.
The priestly garments are made exactly as the Lord commanded.
The tabernacle is set up, and the glory of the Lord fills it.

3: God reveals his name to Moses: I AM WHO I AM. He is the God who simply is, and who has heard the cry of his people.
12: The blood of a spotless lamb protects Israel's homes on the night of death. Jesus, the Lamb of God, gives his own blood at Passover to save the world.
14: God opens a path through the sea and frees his people from slavery. The early Christians saw in it a picture of baptism, which frees us from sin.
16: God feeds his people with bread from heaven every day. Jesus later calls himself the true bread come down from heaven.
20: At Sinai God gives his people the Ten Commandments, the heart of his covenant. They show how to love God and neighbour.
24: Moses seals the covenant by sprinkling the people with blood. At the Last Supper Jesus speaks of the new covenant in his blood.
32: While Moses is on the mountain, the people make an idol. Moses pleads for them, and God shows his mercy.
40: God's glory fills the tabernacle, his tent among his people. John's Gospel says the Word became flesh and pitched his tent among us.
